subject: File::Spec shims had drifted apart in BOTH directions (splitpath no_file ignored → op/chdir.t ran 2 tests perl skips)
description:
DONE s319.  lib/File/Spec.pm and lib/File/Spec/Functions.pm each implemented
all 13 functions independently, and the copies disagreed — in both directions,
so neither was simply "the good one":

  behaviour                     real perl      File::Spec.pm   Functions.pm
  splitpath($p,1) -> dir        whole path     CORRECT         WRONG (stripped
                                                               the last component)
  rel2abs('.')                  cwd            WRONG ("$cwd/.")  CORRECT
  catdir()                      ''             WRONG ('/')     WRONG ('/')
  file_name_is_absolute('x')    '' (not 0)     WRONG (0)       WRONG (0)

THE SPLITPATH ONE CHANGED TEST CONTROL FLOW, silently: t/op/chdir.t asks "is my
cwd named t?" via `(splitdir((splitpath(abs_path,1))[1]))[-1] eq 't'`, then
`skip("Already in t/", 2)`.  Under PCL the directory came back as ".../fake/"
instead of ".../fake/t", so the last component was '' and the skip NEVER FIRED —
PCL then RAN the two tests perl skips and failed both.  Those were shim
artifacts, not PCL defects, and they were sitting in the release signal.
(Diagnosis note: the first probe used File::Spec->splitpath, the METHOD form,
which was correct — the bug only appears via the imported FUNCTION.  Probe the
call form the test actually uses.)

FIX (CLAUDE.md 11): one implementation.  File::Spec.pm is the home and got the
three corrections it was missing; Functions.pm is now thirteen one-line
delegations to it, which is what real File::Spec::Functions is.

VERIFIED: a 13-function parity probe against real perl 5.40.3 is byte-identical.

FALLOUT HANDLED: removing the duplicate exposed that File::Spec.pm's rel2abs
did `require Cwd`, which has never worked under PCL (no Cwd.pm) — task #166.
It now calls the cwd() builtin, with a comment to switch back when #166 lands.

REMAINING op/chdir.t ROWS: t25/t31 ("abs_path() agrees") are separate and still
unexplained — they involve chdir() with only $ENV{HOME}/$ENV{LOGDIR} set.
Re-triage them after this fix; the earlier counts predate it.
